item.title: UK prime minister calls actions of Russian warship reckless but not sinister
item.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer says the crew of a Russian warship of acted recklessly in firing a warning shots near a British yacht in the English Channel

item.title: Sudan’s young women return to international soccer as war and taboos linger
item.description: Sudan's under-17 women's national soccer team has made its first international appearance since civil war erupted in the country

item.title: UK military investigates after Russian warship fires warning shots near yacht in the Channel
item.description: A Russian warship has fired warning shots near a U.K.-registered pleasure yacht in the English Channel

item.title: North Korean leader Kim observes weapons tests from new naval destroyer
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un supervised tests of a nuclear-capable cruise missile and other weapons aboard a new 5,000-ton destroyer, the Kang Kon, according to state media Sunday

item.title: More than 300 children killed in Sudan war in 6 months, UNICEF says
item.description: The U.N. children's agency reports over 300 children have been killed or injured in Sudan in the first six months of the year, mostly from drone strikes

item.title: As war grinds on, Ukrainian climbers build a new outdoor culture inspired by Yosemite
item.description: As Russia’s full-scale invasion enters its fifth year, a group of Ukrainian amateur climbers is trying to build something new: a climbing culture inspired by the sense of community surrounding California’s Yosemite National Park

item.title: A timeline of Marine Le Pen's political career and the rise of the French far right
item.description: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen's political future is on the line as a Paris appeals court rules on her eligibility to stand in the 2027 presidential election
